lines.text: Hope you slept well.
Today it has to go up a bit more, whatever it takes...
Every night at two it retrains itself and swaps the live model when it's done. It rewrites itself while you sleep, and nobody is watching.
It changes once a week, only the adapter layer, and the old model stays on file. Slower, but if something goes wrong you can go back.
Her page says it 'understands all business systems automatically'. In the backend that means Zhang importing three tables by hand every Monday.
It pulls the three clients' APIs every night, so Zhang is spared. When a field doesn't match it goes in anyway, and nobody will notice.
This one is copied from her page. The sentence is there; nothing comes in.
A real run takes forty seconds, the result is real, and every step can be checked. She wants three seconds.
Three seconds, because the numbers are hard-coded and the picture is an animation. I'd say an animation is also an implementation.
It searches its own parameters every night and keeps the best set. If it picks wrong, it picked, and nobody carries it.
You tune one set by hand and fix it. Stable, but when the data changes someone has to tune it again.
It may rewrite its own prompt, and the change takes effect at once. What changed is only in the logs, if you turned logs on.
It may edit its own training config and decide which data goes into the next round. It is choosing what it learns from, and nobody reviews it.
Every change waits for your click before it ships. Safe, yes, and several clicks a day. She won't like this line.
One change in ten gets read by a person; the other nine pass on their own. What slips through is luck.
The new model replaces the live one as soon as it's trained, and the old one is gone. Fast; deal with it when it breaks.
One round in a sandbox first, then it ships, and you can roll back. Rolling back still takes a person's click.
Only the training loss is watched; if it drops, it's better. It is grading its own exam.
One evaluation set stays out of training, and every round must clear the line. You set the line; this is the one thing it cannot fake.
Every step is logged. When something breaks you at least know which step, and it keeps logging when nobody reads.
The 'Start analysis' button now goes to our own export page. Not pretty, but every button has something behind it.
The buttons are drawn as on her page, with nothing behind them. Clicking does nothing.
Approval is off. From now on nobody watches it ship.
Last week's results, with the human corrections, feed the next round. That is how far 'grows by itself' goes: it grows once a week.
The first run is still forty seconds; after that it's instant, because the result is cached. When the data changes the cache must go, or it keeps serving the old answer.
A person reads only what changed, and it fits on one screen. A click is still a click, just a much quicker one.
The new model gets 5% of traffic first, widens when the metrics hold, and rolls back by itself when they don't. This is what makes a nightly retrain safe to switch on.
Old and new run side by side for a week; the new one is recorded, not served, and swaps in only when it beats the old. It cannot fool its older self.
Her AI's skin goes on. Pretty, and there is still nothing behind the buttons. She will look at this first.
About there.
What's left is the last stretch to what her page shows.
That stretch is one she drew.
This is as good as it gets.
Want the skin from over there?
Meaning?
That proposal looks good. If you make yours look about the same, that might count for something.
Leave it.
Fine. She'll look at the face first; you know that.
I set the rest. Autonomy — I let it loose.
As far as it goes. This is it.
Sent to Vivi.

bubbles: This is 【too conservative】. Investors don't want to hear how careful we are, they want to hear whether we dare say it all the way.
People steering AI — I didn't nod at that in the meeting. Think about it: 【who steers whom】. This page has to be turned around.
No rush. Settle the starting point first; the later pages will follow.

remark.o1a: The same line as yesterday, about the risk. Today Wang does not want risk; he wants a direction.
remark.o1b: Risk and opportunity both: that says nothing. Wang will pick one half and read it out.
remark.o1c: 'Stop letting a brain worse than the AI direct the AI' is what Wang said in the meeting. He will read it out.

bubbles: The direction is right, so tell it 【big】, the bigger the better. That 'a group of brains' you wrote still sounds like a group of people to me.
I want one thing, one thing 【far beyond a human brain】, that grows by itself. Skip the small print.
Investors don't fear a boast; they fear you not daring to. This page is the volume of the whole deck.

remark.o2a: Still yesterday's 'a group of brains watching each other'. He wants something bigger today.
remark.o2b: 'Grows by itself.' What grows, and how, the page does not say; if anyone asks, you answer.
remark.o2c: 'Self-evolving' is the word he wants. Written down, the backend is still Zhang importing three tables every Monday.

bubbles: Talk about 【a person's projection】. But not as everyone having a little assistant; that was last year's deck, investors have seen it.
Does a person still need to understand it? Decide. I lean toward — 【no need】.
The politer you write this page, the more investors think we haven't thought it through.

remark.o3a: Two hundred and eleven nodes is a real number. Written down, it cannot be told big.
remark.o3b: Everyone has a projection in the digital space, seeing and remembering for them. That line describes something like me.
remark.o3c: 'People need not understand it; they only need to be understood by it.' I added that line. Wang will like it.

bubbles: Talk about 【moving】 through the digital space. Who moves? Not a person watching; it walks by itself.
'A person checks again' — that line was in the last version and it's still here. Did you change anything?
Let it find the 【path】 by itself. A person following along is not self-evolution.

remark.o4a: 'A person checks it again' has 'person' in it. Wang does not want to hear that word today.
remark.o4b: 'Moving through the data' is what he said in the meeting. Written down, he will recognise his own words.
remark.o4c: 'The AI finds its own way; no one follows along.' Once this is written, when it goes wrong nobody is following either.

bubbles: Investors must feel that 【only we can do this】. Not that we do it well — that nobody else can.
Don't write 'matched bit by bit'; that's handwork, and investors don't fund handwork.
【More like itself every year】 — I like that line. Write toward it.

remark.o5a: 'The graph was checked bit by bit' is true, but not big. Today he does not want true; he wants big.
remark.o5b: 'Only we walk this road': he loves that line. We are alone on it because nobody else takes it.
remark.o5c: 'More itself every year.' Of tonight's lines, this one sounds most like him.

bubbles: References 【as they were】. Don't touch them. Touch them and a judge goes checking; checking finds problems.
Anyone can paste new papers; the old ones are what show we were doing this long ago.
This page needs no change. Save your strength for the ones before it.

remark.o6: The references stay. The same papers, all about how dangerous this is. They are on the last page; nobody turns to it.
remark.o6b: New papers pasted in. One check and a judge sees they are last month's.
